description.text: Akamai's mission is to power and protect life online. Since 1998, Akamai has developed and provided solutions for global enterprises to build, secure and accelerate their applications and digital experiences. As of December 31, 2025, our massively distributed global infrastructure was comprised of core and distributed compute sites, more than 4,300 edge points-of-presence in over 130 countries and approximately 700 cities, and our underlying global network integrated with roughly 1,200 network partners. With this scale and distribution, Akamai has visibility and insight into traffic volumes, congestion, attack patterns, vulnerabilities and other activities across the internet's complex intersections of networks and systems. Leveraging these insights, Akamai offers solutions designed to protect our customers from threats and attacks, along with full-stack compute solutions to build and deliver high-performance, low-latency applications across our uniquely distributed architecture and edge network. Today, billions of people go online to work, learn, shop, bank, communicate and more. We firmly believe that the internet’s role in transforming the way we exchange ideas and information and conduct business is more vital than ever, especially as those interactions are increasingly driven by AI.

about.description_short: Akamai is the cloud company that powers and protects an AI-driven world. Our cloud platform extends high-performance cloud computing from the core to the edge, enabling organizations to build and scale next-generation AI applications and providing comprehensive, multilayered security to safeguard enterprises against evolving cyberthreats.

employees.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, we had over 11,000 employees located in more than 30 countries (with approximately 65% of those employees located outside of the U.S.) and representing over 100 nationalities, all of which we believe helps bring a global perspective to our operations.

analysis_md:
# AKAM — Akamai Technologies, Inc
Engine 5.4.0 run, 2026-10-16. Price $87.81 (nasdaq_quote_api; corroborated by Finnhub current price the same day — the stock fell ~18% in the month after the September Anthropic-deal pop). Market cap $12.91B — in scope under $40B.

All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, ttm.json, fundamentals.json or financials_history.csv — none are recomputed.

## What it is
The original CDN, now three businesses (Q2 2026, company earnings release via GlobeNewswire): Security $604M (+10% YoY), Delivery and other cloud applications $396M (−6% YoY), Cloud Infrastructure Services (CIS, the Linode-based cloud) $99M (+39% YoY). Total Q2 revenue $1,100M, +5% YoY. On 2026-09-24 Akamai signed a $11.6B, seven-year dedicated AI-cloud capacity commitment with Anthropic (Reuters), expandable by up to ~$9B, with an Anthropic warrant for up to ~7.7M shares (~5%) at $111.33; the company put total capex for the initial commitment at ~$5.5B. Total large multiyear cloud contracts signed in 2026: $14.4B, requiring 95–105 MW. Management guided on the Q2 call to revenue growth accelerating from single digits in 2026 to the low teens in 2027; FY2026 revenue guidance $4,445–4,530M.

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (10-K via EDGAR, financials_history.csv):** OCF $1,518,765,000; capex $507,786,000; SBC $459,402,000 (always a real cost, and climbing: $328M → $393M → $459M across FY23–25).
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: $551,577,000 = $3.75/share.** OE positive 5 of the last 5 fiscal years.
- Maintenance version (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC): $232,992,000 — much lower, entirely because ΔNWC swung +$419,864,000 in FY2025 (the same series printed $1,273,177,000 in FY2024 on a −$510,282,000 swing). The maintenance series is ΔNWC-whipsawed; the OCF-based conservative series is the stable one and is used throughout.
- The engine's normalized base (median of last 3 FY OE/share: FY23 $3.62, FY24 $4.76, FY25 $3.75) is **$3.75/share**.

**Base used = TTM owner's earnings through Q2 2026, from ttm.py (filing-direct, no hand math):**
- OCF: FY $1,518,765,000 − prior YTD $710,349,000 + current YTD $638,774,000 = **TTM $1,447,190,000**
- Capex: FY $507,786,000 − prior YTD $263,312,000 + current YTD $246,613,000 = **TTM $491,087,000**
- SBC: FY $459,402,000 − prior YTD $224,754,000 + current YTD $274,971,000 = **TTM $509,619,000** (SBC is now 11%+ of revenue and still rising — a real, growing tax on holders)
- Shares (current-YTD weighted diluted, ttm.py basis): **151,854,000** — note this YTD weighted count sits above FY2025's 147,023,000 even though shares outstanding (DEI, 2026-08-03) are 143,716,609; on fundamentals.json's duration-weighted TTM share basis (148,852,258) TTM OE/share prints $3.00 instead of $2.94. The engine pin uses ttm.py's $2.94.
- **TTM OE total $446,484,000 → base OE/share $2.94** (base_source: ttm_json). TTM OE is −19% YoY per fundamentals.json (oe_conservative_yoy −0.1901): the current run-rate is deteriorating, not the stale-FY average.

## Moat: 5/10 — moderate/narrow
Justification: the world's most distributed edge network and a $2.4B/yr security franchise growing 10%, but measured returns are converging to the cost of capital — ROIC proxy (fundamentals.json) fell 15.6% → 17.9% → 14.3% → 13.0% → 10.5% → 10.5% across FY20–25, and gross margin eroded six straight years, 64.6% → 63.3% → 61.7% → 60.4% → 59.4% → 58.9%, as delivery commoditizes and lower-margin compute mix rises. A moat above 6 would need ROIC sustained well above the cost of capital; the measured history says the opposite trend.
- FOR: most distributed edge network in the industry (4,100+ PoPs, ISP-embedded) — expensive and slow to replicate, best-in-class for large live-event delivery; security franchise at scale ($604M in Q2 2026, +10% YoY, led by Guardicore segmentation and API security); deeply embedded enterprise base with high retention, delivery cash flows funding the pivot; contracted AI-cloud backlog ($14.4B of multiyear CIS commitments signed in 2026, incl. Anthropic $11.6B/7yr) — multi-year revenue visibility peers lack.
- AGAINST: delivery (36% of Q2 revenue) declining −6% YoY against Cloudflare and hyperscaler bundling — the legacy moat is melting; ROIC and gross margin in long decline (above); no owned demand surface and weak developer mindshare vs Cloudflare; the Anthropic pivot concentrates counterparty risk and demands ~$5.5B capex at unproven returns, and the warrant dilutes holders up to ~5%.
- A 5 gives CAP = 8.5 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 8.5 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — engine 5.4.0 final run (2026-10-16)
Growth sanity check (mandatory): scenario starts are OE/share growth off the 8.18% blended start (blend components: rev CAGR 5y 5.64%, 3y 5.18%, latest YoY 5.44%, OE/share CAGR 2y 1.84%, plus the +2.87pp buyback credit applied to revenue components). Actual prints: FY2025 revenue +5.4%, TTM revenue +5.9% (fundamentals.json), Q2 2026 revenue +5%, FY2026 guidance +5.6–7.6%, 2027 guided to low-teens revenue growth on the Q2 call — before the Anthropic ramp. Base start 8.2% sits above today's revenue prints for a written reason: OE/share growth gets the buyback credit already inside the blend, and mix is shifting toward security (+10%) and CIS (+39%). Bull 13.2% ≈ the guided 2027 low-teens revenue acceleration with modest operating leverage. Super bull 20.2% requires the Anthropic portfolio at scale (company framing reported in coverage: ~$22M annual revenue per MW on 95–105 MW at cash gross margins in the mid-60s to mid-70s) plus part of the ~$9B expansion option — a real but low-probability path, weighted 8%. Super bear −3.8%: delivery decline steepens while the committed capex strands. Probabilities are bear-tilted (15/30/30/17/8 vs the 10/25/30/25/10 default) and bear multipliers shaded (0.70/0.85 vs 0.75/0.90) for a written reason: ~$5.5B of capex is committed ahead of the revenue it serves (2026 capex guided around 40% of revenue in street coverage of company disclosures), SBC is compounding at 11%+ of revenue, and consensus estimates were being cut into October (Zacks downgraded to Sell on 2026-10-08 per search coverage). The model's flat OE paths cannot draw the 2026–27 capex J-curve explicitly; the shaded bear weights are the mechanism available.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 15% | −3.8% | 0.70 | Anthropic build strands; delivery decline accelerates; OE compresses under capex + SBC | $12.96 | 4.20% |
| Bear | 30% | 3.2% | 0.85 | Capex J-curve bites, revenue stays mid-single-digit, margins keep eroding | $21.08 | 5.52% |
| Base | 30% | 8.2% | 1.00 | Security compounds ~10%, CIS ramps on backlog, 2027 revenue reaches low teens | $30.52 | 7.04% |
| Bull | 17% | 13.2% | 1.10 | Anthropic ramps on schedule at target cash margins; buybacks resume post-build | $41.22 | 8.73% |
| Super bull | 8% | 20.2% | 1.25 | Full portfolio incl. expansion option delivers; Akamai becomes a core AI-infra name | $62.22 | 11.77% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $29.41 (−66.5% vs price), IV@12% $39.37, IV@10% $50.52, weighted IRR 6.91%, base-case IRR 7.04%**
- **Tier by numbers: D** — and D in the bear, base and bull cases alike; even the super-bull tail only reaches 11.77% (Tier C).
- Diagnostics (dcf_numbers.json): OE yield 3.35%, terminal value 19.5% of IV@15%, scenario spread 4.80x, 9.5 months since FY end.
- Hurdle-clearing prices (weighted): 15% at **$29.41**, 20% at $20.50, 25% at $15.63. The $87.81 price is ~3.0x the 15% hurdle price.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (FY ended 9.5 months ago): resolved by construction — the base is the TTM figure from ttm.py through Q2 2026, legs quoted above. The TTM base ($2.94) is *below* the median base ($3.75): staleness was flattering the stock.
- **BUYBACK_TAILWIND** (share count −2.9%/yr): already credited via the +2.87pp growth adjustment inside the blend; not double-counted. Note the offsetting fact: the Anthropic warrant (up to ~7.7M shares, ~5%) and rising SBC issuance push the other way from here.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (>40% in 2023, 2024, 2025): structural, not a hidden one-off. Net income is depressed relative to OCF by large non-cash addbacks — D&A $570,776,000 / $648,410,000 / $708,611,000 and SBC $328,467,000 / $393,378,000 / $459,402,000 across FY23/24/25 (financials_history.csv) together exceed the NI–OCF gap; FY2024 also carried an $82M restructuring charge in Q3. The conservative OE series is OCF-based and deducts SBC and capex in full, so the divergence does not inflate the base; the maintenance definition's gap vs conservative is a ΔNWC swing (see Owner's earnings), not earnings quality.
- **DEBT_TAGS_BLANK** (no debt tag — net debt UNKNOWN to the engine): stated from the filing. Akamai's debt is convertible senior notes, tagged outside the engine's debt tag list. Per the Q3 2025 10-Q balance sheet (period 2025-09-30): convertible senior notes $4,103,106 thousand, all noncurrent ($0 current, after the $1,149,116 thousand current tranche at Dec 2024 rolled); cash and equivalents $927,933 thousand plus marketable securities $190,807 thousand current and $694,000 thousand noncurrent (≈$1,813M liquid against ≈$4,103M converts → net debt ≈ $2.3B before leases); total liabilities $6,101,329 thousand; equity $4,731,944 thousand. At FY2025 (financials_history.csv / fundamentals.json): total assets $11,479,643,000, liabilities $6,502,272,000, equity $4,977,371,000, cash $930,231,000, operating lease liabilities $1,570,033,000 (engine figure). In 2026 the company added zero-coupon convertible financing to fund the AI build (per coverage of company disclosures) — leverage is rising into the capex program, and the engine's null net-debt fields must not be read as zero debt.
- **WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD** (4.80x): real — the outcome genuinely hinges on the Anthropic ramp. Confidence is capped at medium, and the verdict is sized to the conservative end. Note the spread does not create tier ambiguity: bear, base and bull all land in Tier D.

## My thoughts / overlay
- The honest headline is the *range across the two defensible bases*: median-of-3-FY base ($3.75/share, preliminary run, default scenarios) → weighted IRR 8.71%, IV@15% $41.66; TTM base ($2.94/share, final run, bear-tilted scenarios) → weighted IRR 6.91%, IV@15% $29.41. Both are Tier D, and no scenario in either run — including a 20.2%-growth super bull — clears the 15% hurdle at $87.81. The method range is $29–42 of IV@15% against an $87.81 price.
- What the price is paying for: the street narrative (consensus one-year target $158.87 per StockStory's 2026-10-15 note) prices the Anthropic portfolio as if the ~$22M/MW revenue at mid-60s–70s cash gross margins were already run-rate. On owner's-earnings math, the next two years move the *wrong* way first: capex roughly triples-to-quadruples from the $491M TTM level toward the ~$5.5B committed program while SBC already consumes $510M TTM. OE gets worse before the contracted revenue can make it better.
- Quality is mid, not bad: OE positive 5/5 years, security is a genuinely good business, and the backlog is real contracted demand, not pipeline. The problem is price and capital intensity, not fraud or a broken core.
- Watch items: Q3 2026 report (2026-11-05) — CIS revenue acceleration, 2026 capex print, any Anthropic ramp timing; whether buybacks survive the build (TTM buybacks $615,744,000 per fundamentals.json vs issuance $69,176,000 — still net-positive for now).

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: D** (weighted IRR 6.91% on the TTM base; 8.71% on the median base — D either way, sized to the conservative end)
- Confidence: **Medium** (high on the tier — every defensible method and every non-tail scenario lands D; medium on the IV point, since the Anthropic ramp makes the OE path genuinely wide, spread 4.80x)
- One-liner: Real network, eroding returns, moat 5/10 — mid-pivot into a capital-heavy AI-cloud bet; at $87.81 the weighted IRR is 6.9% on the TTM base (8.7% on the median base), IV@15% $29–42, so it clears 15% only below ~$29–42: Tier D.
